title: The day after
hook: as the Prophet ﷺ is prepared for burial, the Ansar and the Muhajirun meet at the portico of Banu Sa'idah

segments.voice: Yesterday, Block B close: the end of the block on the companions. Your line was: ordinary people, extraordinary faith. Whose story did you tell? Today a new block begins, and those same people face the day the Prophet died. Day eight hundred sixty-three.

In a small room beside the mosque in Medina, the body of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, lies still. His family are with him. Outside, the city is in shock. Some people cannot accept it. And a short walk away, under a roofed shelter that belongs to a clan called Banu Sa'idah, men of the Ansar are gathering. They have a question no one in this community has ever had to answer. He is gone. Who leads us now? Today: the day after.
screen: `HIS FAMILY PREPARE HIM.` → `THE CITY IN SHOCK.` → `A GATHERING UNDER A ROOF.`

segments.voice: Sahih al-Bukhari, in a report from Aisha, gives us the hours. When the news spreads, Umar ibn al-Khattab stands up and insists the Prophet has not died. Then Abu Bakr arrives from outside the city. He goes in, uncovers the Prophet's face, kisses him, and says that God will not make him taste death twice. He comes out and speaks to the crowd. Whoever worshipped Muhammad, he says, Muhammad has died. Whoever worships God, God is living and does not die. Then he recites a verse of Surah Al Imran: Muhammad is only a messenger, and messengers passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Ibn Abbas, in a report Bukhari places alongside hers, says it was as if people had never heard the verse until that moment. Meanwhile the Ansar, the people of Medina who had taken the Prophet in, gather at the saqifah of Banu Sa'idah, the roofed portico, around Sa'd ibn Ubadah. Their first proposal, in Bukhari's report, is simple and fair to their eyes: a leader from us, and a leader from you, the Muhajirun who came from Mecca. Word reaches Abu Bakr and Umar, and they go, with Abu Ubaydah. What happens there, and what it means, is where Muslims' memories divide. Sunni Muslims tell it one way, and tomorrow is theirs. Shia Muslims tell it another, and the day after belongs to them. Today, stay with the hour before any answer. A community has lost the one who received revelation. The family is with his body. Grief and fear and duty are all in the air at once. And everyone is asking the same two words.
screen: `UMAR: HE HAS NOT DIED.` · `ABU BAKR: GOD IS LIVING.` · `THE ANSAR GATHER AT THE SAQIFAH.` · `A LEADER FROM US, AND FROM YOU.` · then, large: `WHAT NOW?`

segments.voice: The practice: sit with the sudden loss of a leader. Sit still for a moment, and let your breath find its pace. Remember a time someone who held things together was suddenly gone. A parent. A coach. A boss. An imam or teacher. Notice what that hour was like. The shock. The practical questions arriving before the grief had room. People reacting in different ways at once. Breathe in, and let both be true: the loss, and the need to go on. Breathe out, without rushing to an answer. If you pray, you can pray for those who lead your community, and for those who grieve. The bell holds the time.
The day after. The day the Prophet died, when his family stayed with his body and the Ansar met at the portico of Banu Sa'idah to ask who would lead. Today's word.
Your line: what now? Today, when something ends, pause before you answer that question, and let the loss be named first. Day eight hundred sixty-three.

howItsDone: Muslims remember the Prophet's death through the reports of that day, and Abu Bakr's words, that God is living and does not die, are quoted at times of loss.

fork.setup: you're one of the Ansar. the Prophet has just died, and Medina is in shock. what do you do?
options: gather at the saqifah and propose a leader from each side.
fork.reveal: Bukhari reports the Ansar gathered with Sa'd ibn Ubadah and proposed: a leader from us, and a leader from you.

original.note: Arabic: a roofed shelter or portico; the saqifah of Banu Sa'idah.

trapdoor: what you thought: after the Prophet died, the next leader was simply obvious to everyone.
what it means: grief, disbelief and an urgent question all at once, with the Ansar gathering at the saqifah.
what a scholar hears: Aisha's report in Bukhari, Abu Bakr's recitation of Al Imran 144, and the proposal: a leader from us, a leader from you.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3667–3668 (Aisha: Umar's denial, Abu Bakr's words and recitation, the Ansar at the saqifah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 1241–1242 (Ibn Abbas: it was as if people did not know the verse until Abu Bakr recited it)

notes: Hadith numbers cited from memory: confirm Bukhari 3667–3668. Abu Bakr's 'God will not make you taste death twice' is paraphrased.
Qur'an 3:144 paraphrased rather than quoted from Pickthall; a Keeper may substitute Pickthall's exact wording.

That the family (Ali, al-Abbas and others) were preparing the body while the saqifah met is widely reported in the sira and is part of the outline's hook; the script says 'his family' without names. Confirm.
This day deliberately stops before the outcome; 864 and 865 give the Sunni and Shia tellings. Please check that today's wording is acceptable to both.
The fork asks only what the Ansar did, to avoid prejudging the Shia position on designation; confirm.

Editor pass: the line 'as if people had never heard the verse' is Ibn Abbas's words (Bukhari 1242, also 4454), not Aisha's; reattributed and cited (numbers from memory, confirm). Cut 'their elder' for Sa'd ibn Ubadah (not in the cited report); cut 'often' from howItsDone; varied the practice opener.

Audit pass (2026-10-01): Whether the washing happened during the saqifah meeting is contested (Ibn Ishaq places the preparation of the body after the pledge, on the Tuesday; Shia histories place Ali at the washing during it). The narrator no longer states either timeline as fact: 'preparing him for burial' / 'washing his body' changed to the family being with him. Review's unsourced superlative 'their hardest day' cut. The outline hook still says 'as the Prophet is prepared for burial'; suggest the index soften it. Keepers from both traditions: confirm.
